summary: A branch is a separate line of commits. You can try a change on a branch while main stays as it was.
notes: A branch is a name that points at a commit. Each new commit moves the current branch forward.
git switch -c name creates and switches in one step. git switch name moves to a branch that already exists.
Older tutorials use git checkout -b name. It does the same thing as git switch -c name.
pitfall: Switching with uncommitted changes that conflict with the other branch fails with "Your local changes ... would be overwritten". Commit or stash first.
setup_note: Starts in a repository with two commits on main.
setup:
cat > gradebook.py <<'EOF'
scores = [88, 92, 79, 95]
average = sum(scores) / len(scores)
print("Average:", average)
EOF

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Gradebook
Quiz scores for Period 3.
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add gradebook script"

cat > scores.csv <<'EOF'
name,score
Ava,88
Liam,92
Noah,79
Zoe,95
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add quiz scores"
